Repository coding-agent instructions. Follow `RULES.md` strictly; repo tooling and explicit user instructions win. Start with task-relevant files; for unclear requests, inspect top-level docs (`README.md`, manifests, module READMEs). Tasks may be architectural, debugging, refactoring, review, release, or documentation.

Read every file you modify in full before editing. Do not remove, rename, or downgrade intentional functionality unless the user explicitly asked for it. Do not “fix” dependency or type problems by deleting behavior or weakening checks. Keep diffs tight; avoid unrelated refactors and formatting-only churn. Run repository validation commands required by `RULES.md`; treat formatter, lint, warnings-as-errors, tests, and coverage as design constraints. Do not bypass hooks, checks, or validation steps. Never use `--no-verify`.

Never commit unless the user explicitly asks. If committing, commit only files changed in this session; use explicit paths; run `git status` and verify only intended files are staged. `git add <specific-file-paths>` `git pull --rebase` `git reset --hard` `git clean -fd` `git commit --no-verify`. Include `fixes #<number>` or `closes #<number>` when applicable.

Protect other agents’ changes. Resolve conflicts only in files you actually changed. If a conflict appears in untouched files, stop and ask the user. Read full issues including comments. Analyze PRs before local changes. Do not open PRs, merge, or close anything unless explicitly asked.

Keep responses concise, direct, and technical. No emojis in commits, issues, PR comments, or code comments unless explicitly asked.

Store transient context under `.llm/{DIR}/`; choose `{DIR}` to avoid collisions. Do not use `.context/`. Treat `.llm/` as disposable, untracked state; promote durable documentation explicitly. `WORKFLOW.md` governs workflow; `RELEASING.md` governs releases.
